Earlier modules each introduced one family of models: moving agents, fields that spread, random processes, networks and discrete rules. Real systems rarely stay inside one family. This module collects optional examples in which **two ideas are coupled** in one model, and asks what the coupling adds that neither part has alone.

# Examples

**Agents and a spreading field**

[Squid Ink: Hiding in a Cloud](squid-ink.qmd){.btn .btn-primary}

A school of fish (collective motion, [Module 2](../collective-behaviour/index.qmd)) hunts a squid that releases ink (a field that spreads and fades, as in [Module 4](../pattern-formation/index.qmd)). The ink changes what the fish can see, and what the fish see changes how they move.

# A recipe for your own combination

1. Pick two models you know and name the **variable that each one exposes**: a position for an agent, a concentration for a field.
2. Choose the **coupling**: which variable of one model enters a rule of the other, and in which direction? One direction is a good start.
3. Keep every new parameter on a **dial** you can switch off, so that you can compare with the uncoupled models.
4. Run the control first, then change one parameter at a time and report the mean and a confidence interval over many seeds.
